title: Storage and data request path
description: Canonical Module 1 path from client to durable stores and derived views. PostgreSQL is the default primary. DynamoDB is a selectable alternative primary, not a replica of Postgres. Redis is a derived cache hop.
assumptions: Single-region unless a node says otherwise.
Synchronous edges wait for a response within the caller timeout. Asynchronous edges enqueue and return before the sink commits.
Postgres streaming replica is optional and is never a second primary.
DynamoDB is an alternative item primary, not a SQL replica of PostgreSQL.
Failover is not instantaneous, lossless, or transparent. Fencing and UNKNOWN in-flight outcomes are in the database-failover walkthrough.

nodes.title: Client
nodes.summary: Issues HTTPS reads and writes. Timeouts are UNKNOWN, not failed commits. Writes need idempotency keys.

detail.consistency: UI state is not a consistency boundary.
detail.durability: None. Retrying a write without an idempotency key can double-apply.
detail.recovery: Retry with the same idempotency key; do not assume the server rolled back.

nodes.title: DNS
nodes.summary: Resolves hostname to edge or origin. TTL cache can send traffic to a drained VIP. DNS is not fencing.

detail.consistency: Cached answers can be stale for the TTL.
detail.failure: NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or stale VIP after failover.
detail.recovery: Short TTL plus health-checked records; still not a lock.

nodes.title: CDN
nodes.summary: Optional derived cache for cacheable GETs. Not on the TokenX ledger write path.

detail.consistency: TTL / explicit versioning. Stale-if-error is a product choice.
detail.failure: Origin shield outage or poisoned cache entry.
detail.recovery: Purge by key; fall back to origin; do not serve ledger balances from CDN.

nodes.title: WAF
nodes.summary: Optional filter. Fail-open vs fail-closed is an availability decision. Owns no business state.

detail.failure: False positives or fail-open under overload.
detail.recovery: Rule rollback; bypass is a security incident, not a data repair.

nodes.title: Load balancer
nodes.summary: Spreads connections. Health checks are liveness, not proof the primary is writable.

detail.consistency: Sticky sessions do not create read-your-writes on a replica.
detail.failure: Unhealthy targets, slow drain, or health-check false healthy.
detail.recovery: Deregister, drain, and fail connections that still hit a fenced primary.

nodes.title: API gateway
nodes.summary: Auth, rate limit, routing. Rate-limit counters in Redis are derived, not the ledger.

detail.consistency: Authn tokens and limit counters are eventually consistent across gateway replicas unless a central store is specified.
detail.durability: Request logs are not commit proof.
detail.failure: 429 vs timeout. Timeout is UNKNOWN to the client.
detail.recovery: Shed load; do not auto-replay UNKNOWN writes.

nodes.title: Application service
nodes.summary: Orchestrates idempotency lookup and cache policy. Crash after commit and before response is UNKNOWN.

detail.consistency: Process memory is not a consistency boundary.
detail.failure: OOM, deploy, or timeout holding a DB connection.
detail.recovery: Idempotent retry; never hold a SQL transaction across an HTTP call.

nodes.title: Redis
nodes.summary: Default cache-aside hop. RDB/AOF does not make Redis the system of record for TokenX balances.

detail.consistency: Cached values can be stale. Replica reads are asynchronously lagged.
detail.durability: Optional RDB/AOF. Restart can lose recent writes even with AOF depending on fsync policy.
detail.failure: Flush, OOM eviction, or split-brain under Sentinel/cluster misconfig.
detail.recovery: Rebuild from the primary. TokenX money paths fail closed on uncertain freshness; ad-click dashboards may fail open on labeled stale reads.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL primary
nodes.summary: Default relational primary. Durability is WAL fsync plus replica acknowledgement policy. Failover needs fencing.

detail.consistency: Default isolation is READ COMMITTED (per-statement snapshots, not session SI). Replicas lag.
detail.durability: Defined by synchronous_commit and whether a standby acknowledged the WAL flush.
detail.failure: Primary crash, disk full, or split-brain if two writers exist.
detail.recovery: Fence the old writer, promote a replica with the latest eligible WAL, increment timeline; in-flight commits may be UNKNOWN.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL replica
nodes.summary: Optional derived read. Applied WAL position defines freshness. Not a second primary.

detail.consistency: Read-your-writes only with a position token on this timeline.
detail.durability: Replica flush is not a client commit unless the primary waited for it.
detail.failure: Lag, WAL recycle forcing rebuild, or accidental promotion without fencing.

nodes.title: DynamoDB
nodes.summary: Alternative item primary. Default reads are eventually consistent. Strongly consistent reads are same-region and are not cluster-wide linearizability.

detail.consistency: Eventual by default. ConsistentRead returns the same-region latest committed item, not a Cassandra-style quorum and not global linearizability. Default global tables are last-writer-wins; multi-Region strong consistency is a named table setting, not the default.
detail.durability: Acknowledged writes are replicated across Availability Zones; there is no user-replayable WAL.
detail.failure: Hot partition, region impairment, or conflicting multi-region writes.
detail.recovery: Conditional writes / transactions for occupancy; do not LWW TokenX balances across regions.

nodes.title: Outbox and workers
nodes.product: Transactional outbox plus optional log (Kafka-class, not required in Phase A)
nodes.summary: Async fan-out after primary commit. Not a second source of money. Kafka durability still needs RF/acks/ISR named.

detail.consistency: At-least-once to consumers. Order is per partition key, not global.
detail.durability: Only after the outbox row or Kafka produce is acknowledged under the named config.
detail.failure: Producer timeout, ISR shrink, or consumer lag.
detail.recovery: Replay committed outbox/journal only; request logs without commit are UNKNOWN.

nodes.title: Workers
nodes.summary: At-least-once consumers for search, warehouses, notifications. Must not become a second TokenX writer.

detail.durability: Consumer offset is not the business commit.
detail.failure: Poison messages, lag, or dual processing during rebalance.
detail.recovery: DLQ + replay; fence work with owner/epoch if needed.

nodes.title: Object storage
nodes.summary: Authoritative for immutable object bytes once PUT is acknowledged. Ledger rows stay in the primary DB.

detail.consistency: Same-region object CRUD and LIST are strongly consistent. Cross-region replication is still asynchronous.
detail.durability: Storage class / replication configuration, not infinite.
detail.failure: Slow PUT, partial multipart, or restore delay from Glacier-class.
detail.recovery: Checksum and retry multipart; metadata in the DB is the catalog.

nodes.title: OpenSearch
nodes.summary: Rebuildable search index. Near-real-time refresh is not a commit. Never spend from search hits.

detail.consistency: Near-real-time, not read-your-writes unless you refresh and wait.
detail.durability: Replica shards; still derived from the primary.
detail.failure: Yellow/red cluster, mapping explosion, or lagging ingest.
detail.recovery: Reindex from the source of truth.

nodes.title: Observability
nodes.summary: Derived telemetry for detection. Missing spans do not mean missing commits.

detail.recovery: Use it to detect lag and failover; repair from WAL/backups, not from logs alone.
